disease_label_per_paper: Streptococcus pyogenes sepsis of possible oral origin
presentation_summary: 57-year-old woman was brought to the emergency department after developing confusion and lethargy.
She had right breast pain and swelling associated with high fevers, nausea, vomiting, and chills; exam showed a right-hand abrasion.
Initial vital signs showed temperature 104 F, heart rate 160/min, respiratory rate 22/min, blood pressure 109/58 mmHg, and WBC 8.7 x10^9/L.
She required MICU admission, two vasopressors, 6 L fluid resuscitation, intubation for clinical decline, and later had WBC peak 32.6 x10^9/L with platelets below 50 x10^9/L.
